content.comment_body: Hello, with [product_name] [version_no], including both standard and SIPLUS versions, I would like to know how long the program remains stored after the device loses power. Thank you.
Welcome to the forum. The program remains preserved if the power supply is interrupted, since it is stored in flash memory. Only dynamic, non-retentive real-time data will be lost.
While we're discussing this, could you clarify what counts as real-time retentive data, and how long such data is retained? Please advise.

This refers to data generated during program execution, such as status states for digital RS memories (when retentivity is not enabled), analog values in analog flags, etc. Retentivity can be activated for certain blocks, but not for all.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are asking about memory retention in [product_name] [version_no] devices after a power outage. The discussion distinguishes between persistent program storage in flash memory and non-retentive runtime data, noting that only specific block data can be made retentive. The explanations help users better understand which information remains after power loss and affect perceptions of product reliability.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the device to keep the stored program following power loss, and seek clarification about the retention of dynamic or runtime data, specifically which types of such data will remain available after power is restored.
